architectures.label: Feature-Sliced Design
architectures.description: Each layer uses only the layers below it; slices of one layer don't use each other (entities only through @x)

layers.label: App
layers.description: Starts the app: routes, the store, the site's frame, styles

layers.label: Pages
layers.description: One slice per page, with what only that page uses

layers.label: Widgets
layers.description: Big self-contained blocks: the header, the footer, the background, page transitions

layers.label: Features
layers.description: What a visitor or the admin does: switching the theme, subscribing, accepting the terms…

layers.label: Entities
layers.description: The things the site is about: the session, the site, apps, videos, the terms

layers.label: Shared
layers.description: No business: the API service, UI kit, strings, helpers

architectures.label: Vertical slices
architectures.description: Every endpoint is a slice (an IEndpoint) in its feature's folder; slices never use each other; Common knows no feature

layers.label: Features
layers.description: A folder per feature: its endpoint slices, its tables, and what they share

layers.label: Common
layers.description: The shared kernel: endpoint discovery, paging, proxy headers, encryption

rules.description: Feature-Sliced Design: a layer uses only the layers below it, and slices of a layer don't use each other (entities only through @x)
Vertical slices: Common, the shared kernel, knows no feature
Vertical slices: an endpoint slice never uses another (what two share lives in their feature)
The frontend reaches the backend only through the API service (shared/api): no other slice calls it on its own
Only a feature's own backend reads or writes its tables' entities
